answer: Escrowed provenance trail: each identity must post a unique physical artifact hash (a photographed marble with distinct veining) before transacting, and every transaction appends a signed pigment sample record to that chain. Cloning forces the attacker to acquire and register fresh artifacts, and any reused umber signature pattern flags the whole lineage for freezing pending audit. The per-clone cost is the artifact acquisition plus the forfeited escrow of the entire ancestry chain, which makes the marginal copy strictly negative-EV.
